ETERNAL LOVE WITH LK 28
#lookkaewkamollak #LKPH

🇵🇭 In recent days, the Philippines was struck by two typhoons, bringing heavy rains and severe flooding across the country.

As waters rose, so did the silent suffering of many including the animals left behind.

When PAWS Philippines released an urgent call for help, LKPH members responded immediately (July 25, 2025) — donating in honor of Lookkaew.

To all the Filipino Lookloks who gave so generously and responded to LKPH’s call for donations:
Your kindness, like hers never goes unseen.

This year, 15 typhoons were forecasted. We’re down to 5.
☔ Please don’t leave your pets behind. Include them in your evacuation plans.
And please — take care of yourselves too.

🐾 Thank you, @pawsphilippines , for rescuing and caring for animals affected by the floods. LK Philippines salutes your mission and prays for the safety of all volunteers. 🙏

👑 𝕾𝖎𝖈𝖎𝖑𝖑𝖎𝖆𝖓 𝕲𝖆𝖒𝖇𝖎𝖙 👑
       𝐓𝐇𝐄 𝐌𝐀𝐑𝐂𝐎𝐒
𝐆𝐑𝐀𝐍𝐃 𝐁𝐋𝐔𝐄𝐏𝐑𝐈𝐍𝐓
         🅂🄴🅁🄸🄴🅂

Season 1 
𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑷𝒐𝒘𝒆𝒓 𝑫𝒐𝒄𝒕𝒓𝒊𝒏𝒆
Episode 3
"𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝑴𝒐𝒕𝒉𝒃𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝑶𝒓𝒅𝒆𝒓"

     "𝑻𝒉𝒆𝒚 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒆𝒅 𝒊𝒕 𝒔𝒂𝒇𝒆𝒕𝒚.
     𝑻𝒉𝒆 𝒆𝒏𝒈𝒊𝒏𝒆𝒆𝒓𝒔 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍𝒆𝒅  
     𝒊𝒕 𝒔𝒄𝒊𝒆𝒏𝒄𝒆. 𝑻𝒉𝒆 
     𝒏𝒖𝒎𝒃𝒆𝒓 𝒄𝒂𝒍𝒍 𝒊𝒕 𝒂 
     ⁹𝒎𝒊𝒔𝒕𝒂𝒌𝒆."

𝑴𝒈𝒂 𝑲𝒂-𝑺𝒂𝒌𝒂𝒚,
October 1, 1986.
Six months after EDSA. 

The BNPP — built, completed, and ready — received its death sentence in six words:

"𝙁𝙤𝙧 𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙨𝙤𝙣𝙨 𝙤𝙛 𝙨𝙖𝙛𝙚𝙩𝙮 𝙖𝙣𝙙 𝙚𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙤𝙢𝙮."

That is the entire justification in 
𝙀𝙭𝙚𝙘𝙪𝙩𝙞𝙫𝙚 𝙊𝙧𝙙𝙚𝙧 𝙉𝙤. 55 for one of the most consequential decisions in the history of the 
𝑳𝒖𝒑𝒂𝒏𝒈 𝑻𝒊𝒏𝒖𝒃𝒖𝒂𝒏.

🔹️ The Chernobyl Comparison — 
A Scientific Mismatch

The timing of EO 55 was not coincidental. 

Aquino's order came months after the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in the Soviet Union.

Here is what the critics never tell you:

𝘾𝙝𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙤𝙗𝙮𝙡 𝙬𝙖𝙨 𝙖 𝙎𝙤𝙫𝙞𝙚𝙩 𝙍𝘽𝙈𝙆 𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙘𝙩𝙤𝙧  -𝙜𝙧𝙖𝙥𝙝𝙞𝙩𝙚-𝙢𝙤𝙙𝙚𝙧𝙖𝙩𝙙 𝙙𝙚𝙨𝙞𝙜𝙣 𝙬𝙞𝙩𝙝 𝙣𝙤 𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙩𝙖𝙞𝙣𝙢𝙚𝙣𝙩 𝙨𝙩𝙧𝙪𝙘𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚

None. 

The BNPP was a Westinghouse pressurized water reactor — the same class of technology used safely across the United States, France, Japan, and South Korea.

Comparing Chernobyl to the BNPP is the scientific equivalent of banning all aircraft because the Hindenburg caught fire. 

They are not the same technology. 

They are not the same risk.

🔹️ What the DOST Said — The Government's Own Scientists

Dr. Carlo Arcilla, Director of the Philippine Nuclear Research Institute under the Department of Science and Technology, stated plainly that the two reasons cited for mothballing the BNPP — a nearby volcano and an earthquake fault line — were both "𝙛𝙖𝙠𝙚 𝙣𝙚𝙬𝙨."

He noted that Laguna de Bay is also a volcano — younger than Mount Natib — and asked: 

"Are you afraid of Laguna de Bay?"

The BNPP was built to withstand a 0.4G seismic shield and can cope with the crash of a 747 airplane.

The safety arguments were not science. 

They were politics wearing a lab coat.

🔹️ The Hawaii Conversation — February 1989

Three years after 
EO 55 — with the Philippines already drowning in 8-hour blackouts — a dying 𝑭𝒆𝒓𝒅𝒊𝒏𝒂𝒏𝒅 𝑴𝒂𝒓𝒄𝒐𝒔 lay in the ICU of St. Francis Hospital in Honolulu.

Former Vice President Salvador Laurel wrote in his 1998 Manila Bulletin column that on 
February 3, 1989, he visited Marcos in Hawaii. 
Marcos told him:
